A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Sketch-of-Thought research work. All 25 pages, including Appendices A–E, are readable; text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v3 reports original accuracy and token-count experiments, router evaluations, and a human annotation agreement study (Tables 1–5 and 7–10; Appendix C.2).

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark results, router experiments, and human annotation agreement study reported in v3 (Tables 1–5 and 7–10; Appendix C.2).

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B retain identical sketching paradigms, DistilBERT routing, router training, and prompt/exemplar procedures. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 15 primary reasoning datasets, Korean/Italian/German multilingual evaluations, GQA and ScienceQA multimodal evaluations, ensemble scenarios, and human labeling study.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain CoT, CCoT-45, and CoD baselines, CoT-versus-SoT ensemble comparisons, and the same four router architectures in Table 7. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample sizes, model configurations, temperature, accuracy and token-count metrics, and ensemble procedures are identical in Section 3, Sections 4.5–4.7, and Appendices A and D.

E4.justification: The paradigm comparison in Section 4.9/Table 5, router architecture ablation, human-labeling analysis, routing distributions and edge cases, and output examples remain unchanged. Retitling Section 4.3 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain three-run averaging, fixed seed 42, the accuracy/token variability columns in Tables 8–9, and the same significance statement in Section 4.1. Uncertainty reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are identical, including the appendix results. For example, Table 1 reports Qwen-2.5-32B SoT accuracy of 82.30% and 57 output tokens in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and expressions for prompting, sketched reasoning, and routing in Section 2 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about cognitively inspired sketching, adaptive routing, token reductions up to 84%, accuracy preservation, and applicability across domains, languages, and modalities.

C2.justification: Explanations of paradigm effectiveness, multimodal accuracy losses, and router behavior are unchanged, as are the limitations and future-work discussion. Section 4.3 retains its complete interpretation despite its new heading.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, checkpoints, hardware, output parsing, prompts, exemplars, and ensemble instructions are identical. Code, router, and dataset access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to cognitive science, efficient reasoning, and prompt compression remains identical.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 changes from 'Paradigm-Task Alignment' to 'Paradigm-Task Performance'; Section 4.9 retains 'Paradigm-Task Alignment.' The arXiv stamp updates from v3, 16 September 2025, to v4, 24 October 2025. Other text and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–10 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. Rendered-page comparison confirms unchanged layout apart from the heading wording and version/date stamp recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: Renaming Section 4.3 distinguishes it from Section 4.9, providing a small navigation clarification. This editorial adjustment and the version/date update leave the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices unchanged, producing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
